$comment: Path patterns to the follow-up step that editing them makes necessary. Read by hooks/scripts/pipeline-hint.mjs. Patterns are JavaScript regular expressions tested against the edited file path; the first match wins, so order from most specific to least.

rules.hint: Edited the settings model. Three copies of this list have to agree: the fields here, the variables in `.env.example`, and the environment table in README.md. `tests/test_config.py` covers the defaults and the fallback on unparsable values, not the documentation — nothing checks that, so update both by hand.

Edited the OCR core. It must not import `streamlit` — that invariant is what lets the CLI and the tests use it, and it was broken once before by a cache decorator. Detection filtering lives in `_iter_detections` and is shared by extraction and annotation, so a change there moves both. The Go service implements the same rules separately: consider whether `ocr-go/internal/ocr/tesseract.go` needs the same change.

Edited the Streamlit UI. UI strings are Spanish, code and comments English. Anything written under OUTPUT_DIR goes through `safe_stem()` first — upload names are attacker-controlled. `tests/test_app_helpers.py` covers the sanitizing.

Edited the Go OCR engine. `gosseract.Client` is not safe for concurrent use: every request must take a client from the pool via `acquire`/`release` and never share one across goroutines. Verify with `go test -race ./...`, which is the only thing that catches a regression here.

Edited the transport structs. The JSON tags here are the public API shape, and `web/static/js/app.js` reads `total_lines`, `full_text`, `total_boxes` and `download_url` by name. Renaming a tag breaks the frontend silently — no test covers that pair.

Edited a handler. Any path derived from a request goes through `Handler.resolveOutputPath`, and any upload through `parseUpload` (`ParseMultipartForm` alone bounds only in-memory buffering, not body size). Tunables come from `h.cfg`, never `os.Getenv`. Run `go test ./internal/handler`.
Edited the Go module. `go.sum` is not committed, so run `go mod tidy` before building or the gates will report themselves skipped.
Edited the pinned dependencies. `pyproject.toml` carries its own `dependencies` list for the packaged wheel; the two are separate files with no check between them. Update both or say why they differ.

Edited a Dockerfile. The Python image has three stages — `base`, `dev`, `runtime` — and `make test-docker` builds `dev` while compose builds `runtime`; a change to `base` moves both. Nothing in the gates builds an image, so verify by building it.

Edited a git hook. `core.hooksPath` is per-clone and not carried by git, so the change only takes effect after `make hooks` — and never for anyone who has not run it. Test it by piping a message into the script directly rather than by making a throwaway commit.

Edited the changelog. The entry rides in the same commit as the change it describes, never its own — that is the one deliberate exception to committing by concern. Only user-visible and architectural changes belong here; internal churn does not. Never add a version heading outside an authorized release.

Edited CI. The Go job runs `go mod tidy` before vetting because `go.sum` is not committed, and the Python job installs the Tesseract binary so the OCR tests do not skip themselves. Both are load-bearing.
